item.title: Emacs in the Age of Magic
item.description:
📝 When RMS was slumming it at CSAIL, it was considered a major achievement just to have your text editor echo back onto the screen what you just typed. Given how much more pleasant the act of programming was becoming, people thought the rules-based paradigm could, with far fewer man-hours than ENIAC would have required, encode enough of the world to pass itself off as a sentient intelligence. The right programming language for AI surely would have to parallel the inherent recursion of human grammars.
🔗 Read more: https://commandlinesystems.com/magic.txt

item.title: Faster Retrieval for Better, More Efficient RAG
item.description:
📝 Given a query vector, MIPS systems search within a database of millions of candidate key vectors for the one that best matches the query. MIPS as a Support Function What makes MIPS interesting from a machine learning perspective is that it is built on a mathematical structure that had been largely overlooked before this work: The function that maps a query to the largest inner product with any key in a set is the support function of that set, a well-studied object in convex analysis. Second, the gradient of that support function at any query returns the best-matching key itself.
🔗 Read more: https://machinelearning.apple.com/research/faster-retrieval

item.title: IBM Quantum Nighthawk Demonstrates New Levels of Speed and Quality
item.description:
📝 ” Nighthawk r2: Delivering Speed for Real-World Workloads Introduced in September, IBM Quantum Nighthawk r2 delivers up to 100,000 samples per second while supporting accurate computations with more than 7,500 quantum operations on 120 qubits. The quantum advantage experiments IBM and its partners published in July were first run on IBM Quantum Heron, with circuits and results openly available for independent testing through the community-led Quantum Advantage Tracker. Nighthawk r3: Scaling to More Than 1,000 Qubits Building on the performance demonstrated by Nighthawk r2, Nighthawk r3 will extend the same high-speed architecture to larger quantum computers.
🔗 Read more: https://newsroom.ibm.com/2026-11-11-ibm-quantum-nighthawk-demonstrates-new-levels-of-speed-and-quality,-with-plans-to-scale-beyond-1,000-qubits-in-2027
